**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 22 already satisfies the playbook's preferred audit position on every parameter:

| Parameter | Playbook preferred | Document (§22) |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | Once per 12 months | "no more than once in any twelve-month period" (22.1) |
| Notice | 30 days' written | "at least thirty days' prior written notice" (22.1) |
| Timing/disruption | Business hours | "during normal business hours… does not unreasonably disrupt Customer" (22.1) |
| Auditor | Independent, confidentiality-bound | "independent auditor bound by confidentiality"; off-site where practicable (22.1) |
| Cost | Vendor's, unless >5% underpayment | "Vendor bears audit costs unless… underpayment exceeding five percent" (22.2) |
| System access | None | "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly…" (22.2) |

Section 22.3 gives us added protection (findings are our Confidential Information, enforcement-only use, shortfall payment resolves the issue). I also confirmed there is no back-door audit right elsewhere: Section 23 "Records and Customer Assurance" contains only a heading with no operative text, and there are no monitoring, telemetry, premises-inspection or remote-access rights running against us anywhere in the agreement.

One drafting observation, not a playbook issue: the empty Section 23 heading may indicate dropped text — worth confirming with Vendor that nothing was intended there before signature.
